turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, doctor. Um... well, I came in because I can’t seem to stop launching projects. It’s just constant. Work plans, certification schedules for my team... which, honestly, the new vendor we're using for the cybersecurity certs is a total nightmare. I spent half of Tuesday trying to explain to their support guy that their portal doesn't even sync with our single sign-on, which is basic stuff, you know? I mean, I've been an IT manager for a while, and the lack of standard integration these days is wild. 

But anyway, yeah, I'm just always starting things. Like home network upgrades. I was up in the attic running new cable last week and I found this old box of stuff from when I was getting my bachelor's, which got me sending messages to all these old contacts I haven't talked to in years. My old roommate actually lives in Denver now, apparently. But the thing is, doing all this... it gets so intense that I just blow past normal limits. Like, I don't even see it happening until my wife or my director at work has to finally step in and tell me to stop.

symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient describes a constant, intense drive to start numerous work, home, and social projects, exceeding normal limits to the point where others must intervene.

turns.doctor_question: When you're in these periods where you're launching all these projects and pushing past your limits, do you also notice that your mood feels unusually elevated or energetic compared to your normal baseline—like you feel exceptionally good, confident, or like you need very little sleep?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, energetic is... yeah. Some weeks I feel almost electric, honestly. Just completely unstoppable. But then, if there's even a tiny delay, or my wife asks a simple question about what I'm doing, I just snap. It feels like everyone is trying to slow me down on purpose. 

Like, the other day she asked why I had the new mesh network nodes spread out all over the kitchen counter. And I'm just trying to optimize our Wi-Fi coverage, you know? Which we really need because our ISP is terrible. They promised gigabit speeds in our neighborhood two years ago and they still haven't laid the fiber on our street. I actually walked down to where they were trenching a few blocks over to ask the foreman what the hold up was, but he was just a subcontractor. It’s crazy how these big telecoms just outsource everything now. When I first got into tech, companies actually kept their infrastructure teams in-house. You actually knew the guys pulling the cables. Now it's just a race to the bottom for whoever bids lowest on the contract... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Something about sleep?

But yeah, I do get really low sometimes. Just completely drained.

And the Jira boards—don't even get me started on Jira. The permissions are set up so poorly by the enterprise team that half my engineers can't even move their own tickets to the "Done" column without my approval. So I spend half my day just clicking buttons so Dave's metrics look good for upper management. It completely ruins my flow state, you know? Especially when I'm actually trying to build something and I'm in the zone... 

But yeah, to answer your question, those high-energy stretches have been happening for about a year and eight months.
